transcript.text: My Panasonic NN-ST45KWBPQ is sparking inside when I heat soup, little blue flashes on the right-hand wall and a crackling noise. I stopped it. Is it safe?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Stop using the microwave now: switch it off at the socket and unplug it, and don't run it again (not even empty) until we know why it sparked. Never take the outer casing off — parts inside can hold a lethal charge even when it is unplugged. It is not safe to use. You must stop using the microwave immediately and leave it unplugged. Sparking (arcing) with blue flashes and crackling on the right-hand wall is a serious fault that can damage the appliance further and poses a fire risk. The most common cause for this specific symptom is a burnt or damaged waveguide cover (the small rectangular panel on the side wall), but it could also be caused by metal inside. 1. 2. Visually inspect the waveguide cover (the small rectangular panel on the right wall) for any burns, holes, or black marks. Please let me know if you see damage to that cover or find any metal items. Regardless of what you find, given the active arcing hazard, this appliance requires inspection and repair by a qualified engineer before it can be used again.

I've unplugged it and had a look. There's a cardboard-like panel on the right wall with a black burnt spot on it, plus a lot of greasy splatter. There's no metal in there, just a plastic bowl of soup. It also had a slight burnt smell, and once a wisp of smoke came from that spot before I turned it off.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. The burnt spot and greasy splatter on the waveguide cover confirm why it sparked. The grease caused an electrical arc that burned through the protective mica panel; once that is damaged, the microwave will continue to spark and can eventually damage the magnetron (the part that generates heat) or cause a fire. Cleaning it will not fix the fault. It must be replaced by an engineer who has access to the correct replacement part and knows how to fit it safely without exposing you to high-voltage components inside the casing. Please do not attempt to run the microwave again or try to replace the cover yourself (the internal parts hold a lethal charge even when unplugged). Contact a qualified appliance repair engineer to replace the waveguide cover. If they find any secondary damage from the arcing, that will also need addressing.

You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.

The fault they reported is: "sparking inside, blue flashes on the right-hand wall, crackling noise". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
